gen-comfortaa-gf-titillium-web: Friendly geometric Comfortaa draws every stroke like neon tubing, with joins no thinner than its stems and a ring-shaped c. Titillium Web is the sans below, with stroke ends set far apart.
gen-comfortaa-gf-zen-kaku-gothic-antique: Round, neon-tube lettering with a ring-shaped c. Comfortaa carries that stretched, friendly mood while Zen Kaku Gothic Antique, a sans-serif, follows with smooth bends and a t whose crossbar matches its stem.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-alike-angular: Aaargh hits like bent wire, strong and constant in every stroke. Alike Angular thickens gently at the sides of its rounded letters, so paragraphs read traditional and held open.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-andada-pro: Aaargh is commanding, its bowls and stems matched in weight, with a generous entrance into the e's eye. Andada Pro, a serif, brings medium modulation and counters the eye slips through.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-average: Aaargh is all muscle, with no thick-thin contrast to slow the eye. Average, its mouths on the e gaping and its curves swelling like a reed pen, keeps paragraphs literary and approachable.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-cinzel: Commanding Aaargh keeps its tube-like strokes constant in width. Cinzel, a serif with a modest gap between stems and hairlines, loosens the mood with generous spacing and open curves.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-diphylleia: Diphylleia reads bookish and traditional, its apertures staying open at tiny sizes and stems just outweighing hairlines. And Aaargh, with no stroke contrast at all, is where the commanding punch lives.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-donegal-one: Donegal One draws refined curves that leave daylight inside them. Aaargh is best at wire-like, commanding strokes, while the serif is best at subtle weight changes and sturdy thins.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-kameron: Aaargh is bent wire made loud, its lines holding their thickness without a flicker. But Kameron, bookish and editorial, lets its curves lighten toward the ends, which softens the whole arrangement.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-lustria: Blunt, shadow-free strength is what Aaargh does best, with not a hairline in sight. And Lustria does its best work in moderate stem-to-hairline shifts and a wide-mouthed a.
